predecessors.name: Republic of Croatia
predecessors.text: the Serb-majority districts of Croatia, 17,028 km2 at the greatest extent in 1991 (infobox): northern Dalmatia, Lika, Kordun and Banovina, then western and eastern Slavonia

successors.name: Republic of Croatia
successors.text: Western Slavonia retaken in Operation Flash (1-4 May 1995) and the Krajina in Operation Storm (4-7 August 1995), 'about 10,400 km2'

ledger.x: 21 December 1990: the Serb districts of Croatia announce the SAO Krajina.
August 1991: the war for the Krajina begins.
19 December 1991: the Republic of Serbian Krajina is proclaimed.
January 1992: the Sarajevo Agreement ceasefire freezes the front.
26 February 1992: Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Syrmia join.
4 May 1995: Operation Flash ends with all of Western Slavonia in Croatian hands.
7 August 1995: Operation Storm is declared complete 'on the evening of 7 August'; mop-up continued to 14 August.
12 November 1995: the Erdut Agreement ends the Republic.

wars.name: Croatian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Ceasefire in January 1992 with UN Protected Areas; Croatia retook Western Slavonia (Operation Flash, May 1995) and the Krajina (Operation Storm, August 1995); Eastern Slavonia passed to UNTAES (1996-1998) and back to Croatia.

wars.name: Operation Flash
wars.outcome: Croatia took all of Western Slavonia by 4 May 1995.

wars.name: Operation Storm
wars.outcome: Croatia regained about 10,400 km2 in four days (4-7 August 1995); 150,000-200,000 Serbs fled.

certainty.note: A front line frozen by the January 1992 ceasefire and the UN Protected Areas, not a border; the pages give no municipal boundaries, so the cells follow circles.
